thread:
Marta: Heads up — GPU nodes in eu-west-1 failing to finish provisioning for the last ~20m. Root errors show KMS Decrypt denied + audit log upload failures after the egress firewall tighten at ~15:30 UTC. Anyone seen this?

Ryan: We pushed a stricter egress policy (fw-eu-2026) at 15:32 UTC to lock down outbound to only internal infra. Possible we blocked the KMS endpoint and S3 endpoints used for audit logs. Can someone paste a failing node log?

Marta: Pasting error from provisioner logs:
```
[2026-03-18T15:41:02Z] ERROR provisioner: failed to decrypt model artifact key: kms:Decrypt AccessDeniedException for key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01
[2026-03-18T15:41:03Z] WARN uploader: audit log upload failed: connect timeout to s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com:443
```

Carla: quick check: from one of the affected subnets: `curl -v https://kms.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/` returns `curl: (7) Failed to connect` (TCP handshake failing). That points to egress-level block not IAM.

Dinesh: I reproduced with aws cli: `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob --key-id alias/redwood-eu --profile provisioner` -> `An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Decrypt operation: User is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on resource` BUT note two different failure modes: 1) connection refused (egress) and 2) AccessDenied when connection succeeds. We may be hitting both depending on subnet.

InfraBot: Deploy notice — firewall rule fw-eu-2026 applied by Ryan at 2026-03-18T15:32:14Z. Changes: block 0.0.0.0/0 outbound, allow internal CIDR and specific service allowlist (empty).

Sophia: Observed a fleet fallback: provisioning jobs spilled to us-west-2 for ~12m while eu-west backfilled, resulting in increased cross-region egress and instance spin-up. Preliminary cost delta ~+$450/hr. We should keep fallback but limit it while we patch.

Ryan: Proposed mitigation (short window):
1) Add temporary firewall allow rule for `kms.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com:443` and `s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com:443` (rule id fw-eu-allow-temp) to restore provisioning and audit upload.
2) Create VPC endpoints: interface for KMS and gateway for S3 in affected subnets to avoid public egress long-term.
3) Update IAM role `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-provisioner` to explicitly allow `kms:Decrypt` on `arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01` with a `Condition` limiting via `aws:SourceVpc`.
4) Route audit log uploads via the new S3 VPC endpoint to central SIEM.

Carla: Terraform snippet for KMS interface endpoint (will apply to infra repo):
```hcl
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "kms_interface_eu" {
  vpc_id            = var.vpc_id
  service_name      = "com.amazonaws.eu-west-1.kms"
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  subnet_ids        = var.subnet_ids
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.ep-sg.id]
}
```

Marta: I'm going to request the temporary allow now and run a couple of provisioning canaries once the rule is live. Will watch `provisioner.errors` and `audits.upload.failures` dashboards. Tagging @oncall to monitor.

Dinesh: After we verify, follow-up actions:
- Lock down IAM so only the provisioner role can call Decrypt and only from the VPC endpoint id `vpce-0a1b2c3d`.
- Rotate the key alias `alias/redwood-eu` (scheduled) and update secrets for provisioners.
- Add automated SIEM check that verifies each node's audit log landed within 60s of boot.

Sophia: Filing incident INC-2026 for tracking (severity: P2). Add cost buzzer for the cross-region spill.

Marta: Thanks everyone — please post changes and timestamps here. Planning to keep the temp allow for a max of 30 minutes while endpoints are created. :thumbsup:
